segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making time, Dana. I wanted to confirm the final scope before I send the order form over. We have 48 standard seats, 6 admin seats, and the implementation package targeting a May 13 go-live. Is that still right?

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Yep, that's right. The only change is we may add two more standard seats for the finance team, but not until June. So don't include those in the initial contract.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Got it. So initial term starts May 1, 54 total seats, and any adds later would be prorated through the billing tool. The annual subscription comes to $38,880, and implementation is a one-time $4,500.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. And the invoice timing, can you make that net 30? Our AP team won't process anything due on receipt.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes, net 30 is already approved. I checked with deal desk this morning. The invoice would go out on signature, but payment due 30 days after that.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Perfect. Contract term is 12 months, right? We don't want the 24-month version yet.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Correct, 12 months. Renewal language is annual, with 60 days' notice if you don't want to renew. No auto-uplift in year two, just whatever's agreed at renewal.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Good. For implementation, we need data import done by May 6 because our team is in training May 8 and 9.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: That works. I'll put the import deadline in the services notes. We'll need your user list and the export from your current system by April 29 to keep that schedule.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Yeah, we can do April 29. Send the order form to me and copy Marcus in procurement. If legal doesn't have comments, we should be able to sign this week.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Will do. I'll send it today with the pricing sheet attached, and I'll include the seat breakdown so procurement doesn't have to ask again.
